scope: Research-only mechanical, integration and lifecycle gap audit for the representative GEO teaching spacecraft. Recommendations are educational product judgments, not a flight-hardware compliance checklist or a claim about an OPIR implementation.
interpretation: A public standard describes requirements for projects that adopt and tailor it. It does not prove that a named spacecraft contains a particular component. New representative geometry would remain Assumed/as drawn; the stated engineering practice can carry the cited Spec or Reported row.

candidates.gap: The catalog names release devices, hinges, dampers, latches and drive electronics. It does not separately explain how completion is observed. Scanner encoders already exist but do not cover appendage deployment status.
row: Monitor deployment progress and report lock/latch state through telemetry
candidates.applicationJudgment: Add a distinct feedback element in the deployment/control diagram. A drawn switch or position transducer is illustrative; the evidence does not pick a sensor technology for this vehicle.

candidates.componentName: Battery discharge path and recharge-isolation switch
candidates.gap: Present cards cover normal charging, load distribution and protection, but not deliberate end-of-life deactivation.
row: Discharge the battery and prevent renewed charging from the solar array

refs: Final recommendations paragraph following the abuse-test discussion

candidates.applicationJudgment: Draw this within the existing power architecture with an end-of-life annotation. Do not invent a dedicated passivation box, relay count or circuit topology. Explain that operational power-off and permanent retirement serve different purposes.

candidates.componentName: Propellant and pressurant depletion or vent paths
candidates.gap: The feed components and ground service valves exist; stored-energy removal at retirement does not.
row: Remove remaining propellant and pressurant energy; GEO disposal uses an adjacent graveyard orbit

refs: Reducing the amount of space debris; End-of-life passivation

candidates.applicationJudgment: Teach the lifecycle boundary using the existing tank/feed path. A separate passivation valve is architecture-dependent and must not be drawn as universally mandatory. No maneuver or valve-actuation sequence is needed.

candidates.gap: Enclosures are drawn without explaining the transition from atmosphere to vacuum.
row: Venting accommodates ascent depressurization while controlling particle contamination
candidates.applicationJudgment: A representative vent feature adds a useful integration lesson near the optical mechanisms. Retain the sealed-or-pressure-qualified exception; do not add holes indiscriminately to every package or assign vent dimensions.

candidates.gap: Shielding and electrical interfaces are covered; mechanical support of wiring at moving joints is not explicit.
row: Protect electrical connections from harness loads and verify repeatable routing through motion
candidates.applicationJudgment: Add supports to the existing harness descriptions rather than a new scene or standalone harness subsystem. Any clamp, slack loop, bend radius or routing shown remains as drawn.

candidates.gap: Ground-reference connections and cable shields are already cataloged, but the connection can be made visually tangible.
row: Bond the mechanism housing to its mounting ground plane when it contains electrical equipment
candidates.applicationJudgment: Add a strap to the existing grounding explanation. Do not create another parent or claim a mission-specific return-current architecture, resistance or termination scheme.

candidates.gap: Core structure and adapter ring are already named; the boundary between structural attachment and separation hardware deserves clarification.
row: A clamped pair of interface rings can release and separate with springs

refs: Section 10.4.3, circular separation-system and clamp-band paragraphs

candidates.applicationJudgment: Use an optional conceptual inset with explicit SmallSat-source scope. Do not assign a Marman band or spring count to the representative GEO vehicle without a suitable named civil GEO source.

candidates.componentName: Bearing lubricant or lubricating surface and migration barrier
candidates.gap: Bearings and motors are covered, but their vacuum-compatible tribology and proximity to optics are not explained.
row: Qualify lubrication for the mission; contain fluid migration where sensitive equipment requires it
candidates.applicationJudgment: A small annotation is sufficient. Do not assign a lubricant formulation or portray all mechanisms as fluid-lubricated.

deferredOrDoNotAdd.componentName: Launch umbilical disconnect and separation-sense circuit
deferredOrDoNotAdd.reason: Useful future lifecycle explanation, but the directly requested HESSI source timed out and no named GEO interface source was verified here. Do not adopt CubeSat rail switches or a generic pinout.

row: Guard against mission loss from a command executed in the wrong configuration
deferredOrDoNotAdd.reason: A controls note is justified; a specific inhibit count, firing circuit or actuation sequence is neither needed nor established.

deferredOrDoNotAdd.componentName: Drag sail, electrodynamic tether or CubeSat rail deployment switch
deferredOrDoNotAdd.reason: These would conflate distinct mission classes with the representative GEO architecture. An orbit-specific teaching variant requires its own design premise.

deferredOrDoNotAdd.componentName: Dedicated passivation valve or battery-unplugging box
deferredOrDoNotAdd.reason: Required lifecycle functions can use different architectures. The audit supports explaining energy removal and recharge prevention, not naming an unsupported package.

deferredOrDoNotAdd.componentName: Robotic servicing fixture or removal docking target
row: Some prepared spacecraft use coupling interfaces and navigation aids for later removal
deferredOrDoNotAdd.reason: Not established as part of this public GEO/civil-twin premise. Adding one now would imply capability not sourced for the modeled mission.

recommendedProductChange: Complete the existing spacecraft anatomy with deployment feedback, moving-harness support and pressure-equalization details. Add a short retirement view linking power isolation, propulsion stored-energy removal and GEO disposal. Keep life-cycle operations high-level and explicitly representative; most findings belong under current parents rather than requiring new scenes.
validation: This artifact records research decisions only. Candidate references were checked against its verified-source records; implementation and acceptance gates are tracked separately.
